claims.statement: When a mech is on the explored planet, Distant Suns lets you draw an extra card, choose one to resolve, and discard the rest.
claims.conditions: Use it whenever the extra choice is worthwhile; consider what discarding unchosen fragments does to deck cycling.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: The episode also debates declaration timing; this paraphrase does not settle that FAQ interpretation.

claims.statement: Treat exploration as a long-run edge from repeated small gains: collect fragments and attachments rather than expecting every individual card to be exceptional.
claims.conditions: This compounds when you can explore regularly; outcomes remain random and decks change as players draw.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts discuss both a high ceiling and bad-luck games, not guaranteed value.

claims.statement: Favor hazardous and cultural decks while their contents remain valuable; the hosts slightly prefer hazardous, especially early, but call the two close overall.
claims.conditions: Monitor deck depletion and switch to industrial if opponents have already milled the better pools.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: This is the hosts’ qualitative ranking, not a verified evaluation of each edition’s deck list.

claims.statement: If the slice permits, put an early mech on a hazardous planet to combine round-one exploration with Distant Suns selection and the guide’s favored hazardous opportunities.
claims.conditions: A cultural planet remains a workable alternative; do not force the setup at the cost of a better opening.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers want at least one hazardous planet in a Naaz-Rokha slice but acknowledge alternatives.

claims.statement: Garv and Gunn can add an exploration at the end of a player’s turn; using it on yourself can pair that explore with Distant Suns.
claims.conditions: The agent can instead help the player whose turn just ended, so choose the timing and beneficiary deliberately.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts call its timing awkward; transcript name variants are ASR, component reference says Garv and Gunn.

claims.statement: Expect high variance: good exploration runs can produce exceptional value, while poor relic draws can leave a sound game without the hoped-for payoff.
claims.conditions: Keep ordinary scoring and board plans viable even when you invest in repeated exploration.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts give no odds; both favorable and unfavorable outcomes are part of their assessment.

claims.statement: Keep a fragment reserve when possible; spend fragments for a relic or command token when the immediate effect matters, such as enabling a point or important action.
claims.conditions: Balance saving against a present need for a relic, token, or stall; this is not a ban on early conversion.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts give a rough desired reserve, not a required fragment count or schedule.

claims.statement: Black Market Forgery can be a modest, cooperative trade: the recipient uses two matching fragments for a relic, the note returns, and you gain payment or goodwill.
claims.conditions: Price it against the recipient’s likely use and table norms; the hosts suggest a small payment rather than extracting too much.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: They allow higher pricing in a cutthroat meta and mention Obsidian as a special case without fixing a universal price.

claims.statement: Buy opponents’ isolated fragments at an acceptable price; generally avoid selling your own unless you urgently need the value, since your supply supports relic and token options.
claims.conditions: This depends on opponents cooperating and the cost remaining below the value of keeping your own fragments.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: A hostile no-deal table may deny this plan, and the speakers allow selling your fragments in desperation.

claims.statement: Dart and Tai let you explore after taking control of an opponent’s planet, extending the exploration engine into conflict and combining with Distant Suns if a mech is there.
claims.conditions: Use the ability when the capture is worthwhile for scoring or position, rather than attacking solely to trigger an explore.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: The claim that this is unique in the game is the hosts’ comparison, not independently verified.

claims.statement: Hesh and Prit’s hero gives a relic and up to two secondaries from readied or unchosen strategy cards; order the secondaries so one result can enable the next.
claims.conditions: Use it when the relic and secondary effects have a concrete purpose; secondary costs still matter.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: The episode leaves a no-tokens-in-reinforcements case unsettled, so no workaround is asserted here.

claims.statement: Psychoarchaeology, AI Development Algorithm, and found tech skips make many branches accessible; adapt to the slice instead of treating every tempting technology as mandatory.
claims.conditions: Technology choices still depend on resources, objectives, movement needs, and what the map offers.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts stress flexibility but also note real constraints; current prerequisites were not audited.

claims.statement: Consider Cruiser II for an early Custodians attempt or distant control objective; the discussed line continues into basic blue movement tech, with Antimass or Dark Energy Tap chosen for the slice.
claims.conditions: Check rival reach, cruiser and tech affordability, and whether the objective rewards the commitment.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts explicitly say not to force Cruiser II when early Custodians or control objectives are unlikely.

claims.statement: Carrier II is a flexible upgrade when dispersed mechs need reach or an invasion needs extra capacity and fighter hit points; it complements rather than guarantees a safe fight.
claims.conditions: Its value depends on fleet composition, production, and enough support to win in space before landing.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: The guide calls it a favored option, not mandatory, and acknowledges some fleets need more support.

claims.statement: Scanlink Drone Network is unusually valuable alongside mechs because Distant Suns improves selection; add it when repeated exploration is part of the plan.
claims.conditions: Target decks that still contain useful cards and weigh Scanlink against movement, production, and scoring tech.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers describe better odds qualitatively and give no probability calculation.

claims.statement: Dreadnought II can be a practical fleet choice when weak production limits builds, adding durability beside carriers, fighters, and mechs.
claims.conditions: Use it when the fleet needs its movement, capacity, or extra hit points and the economy can fund it.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers call it a natural fallback, not the preferred path in every game.

claims.statement: Solve the weak starting production early: the hosts favor a useful forward dock over automatically double-docking at home, and suggest Sling Relay when the dock cannot meet a build window.
claims.conditions: Construction is attractive when the slice supports a useful dock site; home double-dock is an alternative.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: They present several production fixes and prefer a forward dock in many situations.

claims.statement: Assess round-one Custodians through the real table: the guide describes a demanding mix of technology, cruiser, influence, and cash, with Trade or exploration proceeds potentially closing the gap.
claims.conditions: Take the line only if rivals cannot beat you to it and your resources and speaker position make the attempt plausible.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: The source describes several routes and calls the cruiser a significant cost; amounts are guide-era estimates.

claims.statement: A mech can explore the intended forward-dock planet before Construction; attachments may improve the site, while a DMZ result may make a backup planet preferable.
claims.conditions: Choose a dock location that genuinely fixes production and tolerate the exploration risk.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers present DMZ as a contingency, not a reason to avoid cultural planets altogether.

claims.statement: Do not prioritize Supercharge routinely: it boosts a round of combat rolls, but the hosts doubt it changes close fights enough to justify the cost and call it most attractive when many dice benefit.
claims.conditions: It can be a late defensive purchase when tech is available and better uses for the resources are absent.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: This is a marginal-value opinion, not a claim the tech never matters.

claims.statement: Pre-Fab Arcologies is a late, conditional economy play: repeat exploration can refresh attached planets, but extra income may exceed your ability to produce or spend it.
claims.conditions: Favor it with reliable refreshes, a valuable planet, and enough production; sequence carefully to avoid tactical mistakes.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts recognize strong setups but disagree about the prerequisite and follow-through burden.

claims.statement: Bio-Stims can be worthwhile when a valuable attached or tech-skip planet is available to refresh; the hosts do not favor forcing green tech just to pair it with Pre-Fab Arcologies.
claims.conditions: Consider it after movement and production plans are secure, or when a two-green/two-blue objective makes it convenient.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: Its value depends on planet setup; speakers disagree on its comparative priority.

claims.statement: Transit Diodes can regroup dispersed ground forces after mechs have supported exploration, enabling a later defensive or offensive pivot.
claims.conditions: It is a late supplemental blue-yellow option, not an opening priority; value depends on mech positions.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts like it in an ideal two-color path but do not prescribe a fixed route.

claims.statement: Assault Cannon may surprise opponents because the mech is described as a ship at the start of space combat; the guide suggests a fleet of one carrier and two mechs can trigger it before the ground fight.
claims.conditions: This is a specialized late tech play dependent on the actual fleet, target, reach, and combat timing.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: Treat it as the hosts’ 2023 interpretation, not a current-rules ruling.

claims.statement: Visz El Vir adds a combat die to mechs in its system and has capacity to transport them, amplifying the faction’s strong ground force.
claims.conditions: Plan flagship movement and mech placement together; dispersed mechs may be hard to assemble for a late strike.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts praise the dice output but later note its offensive use can be awkward.

claims.statement: Destroyer II may fit a mech-heavy one-round combat plan when enemy fighters are the obstacle; the guide contrasts its broad anti-fighter use with Cruiser II’s more specialized reach.
claims.conditions: Choose by opponents and targets; Cruiser II can be better when its movement enables an objective or mech-assisted strike.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers qualify the ranking by matchup and disagree somewhat on which upgrade is broadly preferable.

claims.statement: Warsuns are a possible late offensive pivot when tech skips and money leave surplus capacity, not a required part of the baseline kit.
claims.conditions: They become more plausible if you can reposition mechs; Transit Diodes can make the flagship plan more coherent.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: Hosts partly endorse the option but doubt it fills a necessary gap.

claims.statement: Spread mechs across useful exploration sites and protect planets with several attachments, while preserving a route to regroup for a late defense or scoring strike.
claims.conditions: Balance coverage against the threat at the table and the difficulty of assembling a flagship or Warsun attack.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: Both dispersed coverage and the risk of scattered forces appear in the episode.

claims.statement: Watch legendary planets while Shard of the Throne remains available; the hosts prefer not to take on that relic risk casually and describe capturing an opponent’s Shard as one alternative.
claims.conditions: This applies only while the relic and its condition are relevant; a DMZ result can change the calculation.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: The guide does not recommend a blanket ban on legendary planets.

claims.statement: Exploration makes attachment and tech-skip control objectives easier to prepare for, but preparation does not itself meet or score a revealed objective.
claims.conditions: Check the actual threshold and timing when the objective appears; the source discusses access to the needed board state, not automatic completion.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: Hosts use broad terms like “easy” without checking each objective’s exact scoring test.

claims.statement: Keep alternate point routes open through Custodians, relics, and secrets; a favorable game may support a round-four finish, while stage-two objectives are a fallback.
claims.conditions: Continue scoring revealed objectives and reassess the table; the fast-win picture assumes useful relics and timing.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts stress that favorable exploration is not assured and a poor run can lose.

claims.statement: Keep fragments available late when practical: conversion can answer changing token needs, including command-token agendas, so early conversion can be regrettable.
claims.conditions: Spend earlier if a token or relic is immediately necessary; waiting is a hedge, not a strict schedule.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: The source treats agenda effects as risks, not certainties.

claims.statement: Avoid agendas that replace mechs; the hosts see Articles of War as a smaller loss because it prevents the space-capable side while leaving useful mech combat strength.
claims.conditions: Vote in light of opponent abilities and the value of preserving your own mech role.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts qualify Articles of War as acceptable in some circumstances; this is their interpretation.

claims.statement: Keep Garv and Gunn for recurring exploration when possible; Alliance is a smaller negotiable tool for shared exploration, including reciprocal early control deals.
claims.conditions: Trade only when the consideration and board arrangement justify giving up immediate exploration or allowing another player an explore.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts strongly discourage selling the agent but acknowledge an unusually large offer could change the decision.

claims.statement: On a DMZ planet, Garv and Gunn can still offer one exploration whereas Scanlink cannot use the mech-dependent Distant Suns extra-card selection there.
claims.conditions: The agent remains subject to its end-of-turn timing and eligible player; a DMZ planet is not automatically worth exploring.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 287, published 2023-02-22; guide-era advice and component interpretations are not independently checked against current rules.
claims.uncertainty: This is the episode’s interaction interpretation, not an independent rules check.

connections.conditions: A mech on the explored planet enables the faction’s extra-card selection, the core exploration interaction described by the hosts.
The agent can provide another eligible exploration which benefits from a mech on that planet.
Exploring after gaining control of an enemy planet creates a possible refresh opportunity for the late Pre-Fab Arcologies plan.
The flagship adds a combat die to mechs in its system, so placement and movement determine where the bonus applies.
The hosts describe the mech as a ship at space-combat start, creating an Assault Cannon surprise opportunity.
Transit Diodes can regroup mechs dispersed to support exploration for a later defensive or offensive pivot.
Repeated exploration can help refresh planets that make Pre-Fab Arcologies attractive, if the player can spend the income.
